title: Russia-Ukraine War: ISW Assessment for August 15 Highlights Strikes, Frontline Pressure
excerpt: Ukraine targets Savasleyka airfield housing Kinzhal-carrying MiG-31Ks; Russian drone strikes kill civilians including an infant in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.
body:
• Ukraine struck Russia's Savasleyka airfield, home to MiG-31K fighters that carry Kinzhal hypersonic missiles.
  • A Ukrainian drone attack halted oil loadings at Russia's Sheskharis terminal in the Black Sea on August 14.
  • Russian drone strikes killed civilians across multiple Ukrainian oblasts, including a three-month-old baby in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.
  • Frontline activity continued in the Slovyansk, Dobropillya, Kostyantynivka, and Eastern Zaporizhia directions.

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) published its daily Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment for August 15, covering intensified strike campaigns on both sides and continued positional fighting across multiple frontline sectors.

Ukraine's Deep Strikes

Ukrainian forces struck the Savasleyka military airfield in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, which serves as a base for MiG-31K interceptors — the primary carriers of Kinzhal hypersonic missiles used in strikes against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. The Ukrainian General Staff confirmed the attack, which is part of Kyiv's ongoing campaign to degrade Russian aviation capabilities.

Separately, a Ukrainian drone attack on August 14 forced Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal in Novorossiysk to halt loadings, according to Reuters. The terminal handles approximately 700,000 barrels per day and is critical to Russian oil exports through the Black Sea. The strike adds to Ukraine's systematic campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

Russian Strikes on Civilians

Russian forces continued their drone and missile campaign against Ukrainian civilian areas. A three-month-old baby was killed in a Russian drone strike on Marhanets in the Nikopol district of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, with more than 10 people wounded. Additional strikes hit targets across Mykolaiv, Poltava, Odesa, and Zaporizhia oblasts, damaging residential buildings and civilian infrastructure.

The strikes come as Russia is reportedly preparing a large-scale campaign against energy infrastructure in Kyiv City ahead of Ukraine's Independence Day on August 24, according to an earlier ISW assessment citing US intelligence.

Frontline Developments

ISW's maps for August 15 covered the Slovyansk direction, the Dobropillya tactical area, Eastern Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, and Eastern Zaporizhia Oblast — indicating continued fighting in these sectors.

In the Kostyantynivka direction, Russian forces reportedly attempted to bypass Ukrainian defensive positions. In the Lyman area, Ukrainian forces from the 66th Brigade continued clearing operations against Russian positions.

Ukrainian counterattacks in the Oleksandrivka direction continued to present the Russian military command with dilemmas, forcing choices between defending against Ukrainian advances and allocating forces for offensive operations elsewhere, including Russia's spring-summer 2026 offensive against Ukraine's Fortress Belt in Donetsk Oblast.
